analysis: The PR adds only documentation: changelog.d/gemma-tensor-parallel.md (new) and a new 'Gemma 4 tensor-parallel rank memory' section in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, plus a date bump. No source code, keys, attestation, or authorization logic changed. I found no concrete security regression. The changelog describes Gemma 4 TP prompt-prefix caching in memory and in the encrypted SSD tier, restored only when both Macs hold the prefix and surviving restarts. That falls under T-041 (prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle, SEC-035 accepted risk). It describes behavior in unchanged-scope terms ('as the pipeline does'), but the implementation is not in this batch. Unverified: whether the TP prefix entries use the same HMAC-keyed lookup tags, salt scoping, 30-minute TTL and KEK-rooted crypto, and whether the per-rank prefix entries and the inter-Mac sealed link (TB-002 and the cluster channel) keep the same authentication and fail-closed behavior. Persistence across restarts of both Macs extends the cache surface to TP pairs. The next pass should check that the code behind the documented claim keeps T-041's detection_hint constraints. Also unverified is the claim that DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_BATCH_LANES defaults to one request. The memory-budget table is an availability-related accounting claim (the 5.5 GiB conservative activation reserve, prefix memory 'charged nowhere' but dropped first under pressure); it was not verified against the code, and the doc itself says nothing is measured on a pair. The T-041 threat model may need a note that Gemma TP prefix entries are covered, but this cannot be established from docs alone. Escalating as needs_deeper_review is optional; the code diff is outside this batch.
